item.title: Boston History Lesson: Great Molasses Flood
item.description: Around lunchtime on January 15, 1919, a 50-foot-tall molasses tank ruptured and spilled out onto the streets of the North End. According to History.com, more than 2 million gallons of thick liquid poured out like a tsunami wave, reaching speeds of up to 35 miles per hour.
